_doc: The metronome's phase table, IN SHADOW (OPS_METRONOME_PROVE_IN_SHADOW; design/RimMandrake/operations_metronome_strategy_2026-11-02.md §2, §8 step 5). Read by src/RimMandrake/Utils/metronome.py, validated by `metronome.py lint`. Phases run in the order sense, remember, raise, ring, dispatch, chores; a phase is due when beat % every == offset, when it is overdue, or when one of its wall-clock slots is due. budget_s bounds the whole beat; raise and ring (and any overdue phase) are reserved first. Shadow commands only read or write inside {state} (ops_watch's own store there, the Dispatcher's dry tick, restart_reconcile --no-file): nothing rings, raises or files. limit_s values are ESTIMATES (ops_watch: 73 s for all 20 families, so 2 per beat); measure them from beats.jsonl before cutover (step 6); first shadow beats, 2026-11-04: steve+testing 1.5 s, but accounts+codex and disk+timers each overran 15 s, so per-family timing decides the pairing before cutover. chores has no shadow command yet: its four timers stay the owners.

chores.why_no_command: scratch pressure, account plan and usage keep their own timers until cutover
